title: Push and pop in an array-based stack
summary: Treat the end of the array as the top of the stack so both push and pop operate at the end.
context: On the left is the external stack view, with the top above and the bottom below; on the right is a vertical array with the first element at the bottom and the last element at the top. A leftward arrow between them is labeled "Implemented with an array. Exposes stack operations".
description: The array order from first to last element matches the stack order from bottom to top, both read upward in the figure. Gray dashed cells and an ellipsis above the last element are labeled "Unused array slots".
result: In an array-based stack, pushing and popping correspond to appending and deleting at the end of the array; when no resizing is triggered, both take O(1) time without shifting existing elements.

frames.title: Initial stack: last array element 5 is the top
frames.explanation: From first to last element, the initial occupied array is [1, 3, 2, 5], matching the stack from bottom to top with 4 elements in total. First element 1 corresponds to the bottom, and last element 5 corresponds to the top; above 5 are two gray dashed unused slots and an ellipsis.
frames.key_state: Initial occupied array (first to last) [1, 3, 2, 5]; first element 1 is the bottom, last element 5 is the top, with unused slots above.
frames.announcement: The initial array holds 4 active elements [1, 3, 2, 5], with last element 5 as the stack top.

frames.title: Push 4 at the end of the array
frames.explanation: Call push(4), labeled on the right "Add element 4 to the end of the array". A cyan 4 is written into the first unused slot above the previous last element 5, and the "Last element" label moves up to 4. From first to last element, the occupied array is now [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], matching the stack from bottom to top with 5 elements; the first element and stack bottom remain 1, the last element and stack top are 4, and unused slots remain above.
frames.key_state: After push(4): occupied array (first to last) [1, 3, 2, 5, 4]; last element and stack top updated to 4.
frames.announcement: Call push(4) to write 4 into the unused slot at the end of the array; the last element and stack top become 4.

frames.title: Pop 4 from the end of the array
frames.explanation: Call pop(), labeled on the right "Delete the last array element". Remove and return last element 4; its former cell reverts to a gray dashed unused slot, and the "Last element" label moves down to 5. From first to last element, the occupied array returns to [1, 3, 2, 5], matching the stack from bottom to top with 4 elements; the first element and stack bottom are 1, and the last element and stack top are 5.
frames.key_state: After pop() removes and returns last element 4: occupied array (first to last) [1, 3, 2, 5]; last element and stack top restored to 5.
frames.announcement: Call pop() to remove and return last array element 4, restoring the last element and stack top to 5.
